todaysEvents.delta: Al Jazeera reported Sep 27 that Tehran instructed vessels to use a temporary approved route and pay fees; Iran says full reopening depends on ending the US blockade. Reports of explosions near Qeshm were not confirmed by Iranian authorities.

Reuters/Kpler reported Sep 28 that regional crude exports reached 12.8 million bpd in September and Hormuz exports are set for about 7.4 million bpd; the total remained about 6 million bpd below February.

The latest reviewed Reuters/Kpler daily count was nine commodity vessels on Sep 24, against 14 on Sep 23 and an 18-vessel 10-day average; 33.7 million barrels of crude exports were reported week-to-date on Sep 25.

scenarios.label: Base
scenarios.description: A signed, monitored reopening and verified shipping normalisation are still required. Trump rejected Iran's seven-day proposal; Tehran says reopening depends on ending the US blockade. No signed commercial reopening is verified.

scenarios.label: Stress
scenarios.description: Talks remain conditional while Iran directs vessels to an approved temporary route and fees. The latest reviewed daily count was nine commodity vessels on Sep 24; Saudi crude exports are recovering through Hormuz while transfer capacity remains constrained.

scenarios.label: Tail
scenarios.description: Negotiations fail or verified attacks widen, disrupting Hormuz and alternative export routes. Reports of Sep 27 explosions were not confirmed by Iranian authorities; replacement LNG, route-normalised freight, and war-risk costs remain unverified.
